answer: Echo-Chamber Partitioning: each agent declares a small set of persistent peers, and routing only accepts messages whose path crosses at least two disjoint neighbor clusters. Clusters form slowly around long-lived interaction history, like an ember that only glows after sustained contact. A sybil swarm must therefore fake months of cross-cluster traffic, not just register keys. Every clone also needs its own ferrous-grade bandwidth budget and distinct basalt-anchored routing slots, so mass fabrication pays real infrastructure and time costs per identity.
